speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the progression of your symptoms. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or slurred speech recently? And when did these double vision and weakness symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that clarification; the fluctuating weakness and specific eye movement issues are significant. Do you experience any ptosis (drooping eyelids), and do you have a history of thyroid disease or other autoimmune conditions?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Function_Panel, Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies, Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Thyroid_Function_Panel: NORMAL READINGS; Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity, diplopia specifically with upward/downward gaze, and the absence of sensory deficits or muscle wasting makes Myasthenia Gravis the leading diagnosis despite the previous mention of Tuberculosis. The requested antibody and nerve stimulation tests will confirm this.
